entries.title: Add Word, Markdown and plain text files
entries.body: Alongside PDFs and web pages, you can add Word documents (.docx), Markdown files and plain text files to your library, by picking them or dragging them in. The app turns each into an article, and keeps the file you uploaded. Pictures inside Word documents are left out, and the article's Metadata page no longer offers 'View the original' for these files, because what you read is a converted copy.

entries.title: A first-opened article no longer opens Marginalia
entries.body: The first time you open an article on a wide window, it opens on the Chat guide alone; the Marginalia notes beside the text no longer open with it. On a narrow window you see the article alone. There is less on screen the first time you meet a piece.

entries.title: Referee's suggested criteria wait for your own
entries.body: In Referee mode, the suggested criteria appear only after you press Run on a criterion of your own, so the first thing you check is what you chose, not what the app put in front of you. Once they appear, they stay for that article in that tab, even if a run fails.

entries.title: Referee's Claims view is now called Promises
entries.body: The part of Referee mode that was called Claims is now called Promises: what the paper promises up front. The Sources mode uses the word Claims, so the two no longer share a name. Old links and remembered views open Promises, and exports use the new name.

entries.title: Microphone errors say what went wrong
entries.body: When dictation could not open your microphone, it always told you to press the button again, even when the browser had refused permission or there was no microphone. It now says which of those happened. These failures are also reported to us, carrying only the kind of failure and none of your words.
